blocks.text: The Candelabra geoglyph on a sandy slope above the sea near Paracas, Peru
Paracas: the enormous Candelabra geoglyph above the rocky coast
10 January: Islands off Paracas, the Nazca Lines and Lima

Breakfast. In the morning, head to the pier at the Paracas hotel.

Take an open boat or yacht to the islands known as Peru’s ‘mini-Galápagos’. On the way, you can see the Candelabra, an enormous figure etched into a sandy slope and pointing towards the Nazca Desert.

The islands are home to Humboldt penguins, fur seals and many birds. The boat trip lasts about **2 hours**, after which you return to the hotel.

At the scheduled time, transfer to Pisco Airport, about 30 minutes away. Your flight over the Nazca Lines departs from here. These enormous figures on the desert plateau are best seen from the air.

During the flight, you’ll see **12 geoglyphs on the Nazca Plateau and 2 on the Palpa Plateau**, as well as the Ocucaje Valley, where marine fossils around **150 million years old** are found, and other valleys associated with the Paracas and Nazca cultures.

The purpose of the lines and how they were made remain a mystery. One theory suggests they formed a giant astronomical calendar that reflected the patterns of the night sky.

The flight lasts about **1 hour and 40 minutes**. This is a group service, and a guide is not included during the flight.

After the flight, transfer to Lima and check into a **Junior Suite** at **Belmond Miraflores**.

Paracas brings the trip to a close with a different landscape. After green valleys and highlands, you reach the dry Pacific coast, where the desert comes almost to the ocean. The morning boat trip focuses on wildlife, and the afternoon takes you to the archaeological mystery of Nazca. First you see seabirds, penguins and fur seals, then you board a plane for a view of the enormous figures on the desert plateau.
A small plane above a bird geoglyph in the Nazca Desert, Peru
